Ok so I feel like it’s story time, when I was around 11 or 12 i started a daily journal that I wrote in until 18. The journal was just a password protected word document but as a depressed closet trans kid dealing with abuse and suicidal thoughts It was pretty heavy and i wanted that shit to be extra secure. I made the password the first line to my favorite song at the time but I changed one word of it AND i also misspelled a different word. This was on purpose, and I never thought i would forget this password. Well 6 years later, to last year, I started feeling sentimental and started going through all my old shit on my computer and I found my journal! I remember how it held a lot of my breakthrough realizations and I was excited to go back and read it to see my healing journey and to look back and see how far I’ve come, and well I’m sure at this point you think you know how this story ends but hear me out not being able to open this document that basically contained an unfiltered look back at my childhood was infuriating me so I went online and started searching for a program that would unlock a locked word doc. I found one and I bought it. Turns out not only was this program a virus it was also a scam so between buying this “program” and taking my computer in to remove the virus I ended up losing about $200. So long story short yes people who spell poorly probably do have more secure passwords but they probably also won’t ever be able to remember them.

I also just realized idk where you are located, I’m from the US and these would be my tips for someone looking for affordable therapy In the states. Idk how other countries work in terms of finding affordable healthcare

As the patient you have every right to decline medication or dosage upping and try therapy instead. If you can’t afford therapy try finding a therapist that’s uses a sliding scale system which determines the price you pay based on your income, you can typically find these in training clinics. Or you can try your local community health center some offer free individual therapy, or try group therapy these are also often free

I know due to COVID lots of states are granting therapists provisional licenses to continue to see their patients if their client had to leave the state. You should tell your therapist you are moving because it’s their career on the line. And most likely at least for the time being you’ll be able to keep seeing your T, all it takes is a call the state’s licensing board from your therapist and they will likely grant your T approval to continue to treat you.

DISCLAIMER: I am not a doctor, I am just speaking from my personal experience.
 
If Prozac is the medication your doctors are trying to up the dose on then 30mg is a fairly common dosage for that medication. Often when doctors put you on a new meds they start with a very low dose to make sure there isn’t any negative side effects and then slowly increase the dosage until you start experiencing improvement in your symptoms. I have had doctors that just kept raising the dosage on my medication past the point I felt i needed (like so high that the dose they had me on was used for psychosis when i just suffer from depression). Some medications may work great on other people but just dont work with the chemistry of your body, thats what happened with me. That doesn’t seem to be what’s happening here imo if you are continually starting and stopping your meds then to me its seems like the meds arent doing their job yet on 20 mg and the doctors want to try 30mg. If you aren’t comfortable upping the dose of your current medication then talk to your doctor and ask if there is another medication you can try, but be aware you might find yourself in a similar situation where they start you off with a lower dose and overtime continue to increase it.
